pages.title: First principles
pages.text: Start with what you know is true. A boat must float and carry its load. It does not need to look like other boats.
pages.question: Could you invent a new kind of chair?

pages.title: Test your ideas
pages.text: Drop two balls of different weights.
pages.question: Which lands first?

pages.title: Evidence
pages.text: A good test helps us find out if an idea is true. Without air resistance, both balls fall at the same rate.
pages.question: What else could you test?

pages.title: Emergence
pages.text: Watch the birds. Change their rules.
pages.question: Do they need a leader?

pages.title: Emergence
pages.text: Each bird follows a few simple rules. Together, they can form a flock. A big pattern can emerge from small actions.
pages.question: Where else do you see groups forming patterns?

pages.title: Feedback loops
pages.text: Try to keep the room warm, but not too hot.
pages.question: Which setting works better?

pages.title: Feedback
pages.text: A heater warms the room. When the room gets warm enough, the thermostat turns the heater off. The result changes what happens next.
pages.question: What makes you stop eating when you are full?

pages.title: Networks
pages.question: Can you still get to the other side?

pages.title: Networks
pages.text: A network is a group of things joined by links. Extra links can give us other ways to get somewhere.
pages.question: Can you take two different routes home?

pages.title: Exponential growth
pages.text: Grow a pond full of lily pads.
pages.question: When is it half full?

pages.title: Exponential growth
pages.text: Each lily pad makes another. The more pads there are, the more new pads grow each day.
pages.question: What happens if you double four, then double again?

pages.title: Scarcity and choice
pages.text: You have six blocks. Choose what to build.
pages.question: What will you have to leave out?

pages.title: Scarcity
pages.text: We have only so much time, money and material. Choosing one thing can mean giving up another.
pages.question: What would you do with one free hour?

pages.title: Trade-offs
pages.text: Adding bars makes this frame stronger, but also heavier. A trade-off is when getting more of one thing costs you something else.
pages.question: Would you rather have a light bike or a strong one?
